what: Whether the matched mx comparison is biased by the two arms competing for memory
host: Ryzen 7 5800X, 31.9 GB RAM, 16.5 GB free at the time, 6 threads
harness: tools/compare_cpu.py, pinned 215-token excerpt plus 32 forced tokens, 8 alternating pairs
why: llmx copies the 8.7 GB model into the heap and mx maps it, so alternating the arms needs about 17 GB

harness_self_check.note: one binary as both arms; this validates the timing mechanics

finding: Both binaries lose about a fifth of 8B decode to contention: llmx 3.89 -> 4.73 and mx 4.02 -> 4.78. The harness itself is clean, so the paired comparison is not grossly biased, but its absolute rates do not represent single-process use and the size of the 8B decode deficit depends on which condition is read.

8B_decode_deficit.caveat: The uncontended figure compares two separate runs and is NOT paired, which is the comparison the runner warns against; drift between 01:35 and 01:45 could account for part of it.

unchanged: Prefill: llmx is roughly double mx in both conditions on both models.
next: A paired 8B comparison needs either more free memory or arms that do not evict each other; 0.6B pairs cleanly and is unaffected.
